case.question: Should Nabtesco Corporation develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing precision reduction gears, automatic doors, transport equipment and welfare components sold to manufacturers, building owners and transport operators? What evidence would justify that investment?
case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited older home owners and family members considering an automatic opener for a home entrance door were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical opener, installation, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added an independent safety certificate for the door's anti-pinch sensors and an in-home demonstration of the door stopping on contact; the other showed the same opener with its specification sheet. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 deposits for the safety-assurance offer and 32 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether safety assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, that installers would carry the product, or why a rival's home opener left the market. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.
We hold roughly a 60% (Nabtesco’s estimate) share of the domestic market, and about a 20% (Nabtesco’s estimate) share of the global market, for automatic doors for buildings.

These doors are used at a wide range of places, such as office buildings and public and commercial facilities. We have a proven track record also with industrial sites, such as factories and waste treatment facilities.

Nabtesco became the first in the world to develop a microprocessor-controlled intelligent prosthetic knee joint as mobility support equipment. The microprocessor detects the user’s walking speed, adjusts the pneumatic cylinder, and automatically controls the swing speed of the knee joint to help the person walk comfortably and naturally.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited owners of small carpentry workshops and skilled hobby woodworkers were assigned equally to two offers for the same compact CNC router. Both showed the identical machine, working area, price, installation, warranty and delivery time. One offer came with simplified design software and a library of ready-to-cut furniture templates that need no programming; the other came with the standard professional CAD/CAM software. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 deposits for the template-software offer and 32 for the standard-software offer. This tests whether programming complexity changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that a machine at a price these buyers pay could be built, that the market is large enough, or that it fits the company's industrial dealers. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

Constraints: The company's current revenue streams and customer base are primarily B2B, with products sold to manufacturers in various sectors.; The test budget is 20,000 EUR, and the experiment must be completed within 12 weeks.; The analysis must be based solely on publicly available information and company statements.. Who benefits: Biesse and its individual buyer customers.. Test "Differentiated Consumer Proposition Test" between T1; T2. Method: Survey of individual buyers in the wood processing industry. Sample: 500 individuals, 250 each from existing B2B and potential DIY markets. Measure: Intent to purchase specialized machinery, satisfaction with current products, and perceived value of different product features. Predictions: T1: B2C customers in the wood processing industry will show higher intent to purchase and satisfaction with a differentiated consumer proposition.; T2: DIY market participants will exhibit higher intent to purchase and satisfaction with a range of user-friendly, affordable machines.. Decision rule: If the difference in intent to purchase between the B2B and DIY groups is greater than 10%, T1 is supported. If the difference is greater than 15%, T2 is supported.. Cost: 10000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Based on the evidence, Biesse should enter the DIY market with a range of user-friendly, affordable machines designed for home woodworkers. However, before committing to this strategy, a test is recommended to validate the demand and customer preferences in this segment. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 revised: The simulated test result suggests that offering simplified design software with furniture templates does not significantly change the choice of CNC routers among individual buyers in the wood processing industry. This supports T1, which proposes a differentiated consumer proposition, but with a focus on product features rather than software complexity. New claim: Biesse should offer a range of CNC routers with customizable software options, catering to both professional users who need advanced CAD/CAM capabilities and hobbyists who prefer simpler design tools and pre-made templates.. Evidence: SYN-BIESSE-UPDATE.

Recommendation: While the simulated test offers valuable insights, it cannot directly inform decisions about real market demand. Therefore, we recommend a more robust approach: conduct a real market study to understand individual buyer preferences and demand for CNC routers with customizable software. This will provide a solid foundation for Biesse's product development and marketing strategies. Target customer: individual buyers in the wood processing industry, including hobbyists, small workshops, and professional users.. Value proposition: Biesse will position itself as a leader in providing flexible CNC router solutions that cater to a diverse range of individual buyer needs, from hobbyists seeking simplicity to professionals demanding advanced capabilities.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Conduct a comprehensive market study to gather data on individual buyer preferences, software requirements, and pricing expectations for customizable CNC routers.. Uncertainty: The success of Biesse's differentiated consumer proposition depends on accurately understanding the market segments and their specific needs. The company should be prepared to adapt its strategy based on real market feedback.. Would change if: Market research reveals a strong preference for advanced software among professional users.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited owners of small carpentry workshops and skilled hobby woodworkers were assigned equally to two offers for the same compact CNC router. Both showed the identical machine, working area, price, installation, warranty and delivery time. One offer came with simplified design software and a library of ready-to-cut furniture templates that need no programming; the other came with the standard professional CAD/CAM software. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the template-software offer and 72 for the standard-software offer. This tests whether programming complexity changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that a machine at a price these buyers pay could be built, that the market is large enough, or that it fits the company's industrial dealers. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

Both showed the identical products, charging power, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added a free check of the owner's car model and home wiring with a written assurance that the set would work with both; the other listed the same compatibility tables for the owner to check. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a completed purchase not returned within 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 purchases for the checked-compatibility offer and 32 for the self-checked offer. This tests whether compatibility uncertainty changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand beyond that group, the cost of running the checks, or how established wallbox brands would respond. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited hobby 3D-printer owners were assigned equally to two offers for the same diamond-tipped nozzle. Both showed the identical product, price, compatibility list, delivery time and return policy. One offer added a written wear guarantee with a free replacement if the nozzle wore out within two years of printing abrasive filament; the other described the same nozzle as wear resistant without a guarantee. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a completed purchase not returned within 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 purchases for the guaranteed offer and 72 for the standard offer. This tests whether a durability assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show how many hobbyists print abrasive filament, what the guarantee would cost the company, or that cutting-tool customers would follow. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited households in a deposit-return scheme were assigned equally to two offers for returning empty containers. Both paid the identical deposit refund into the same app, with the same fee and payout time. One offer collected bagged containers from the household's door every two weeks; the other asked the household to drop the same bags at a return point in a nearby store. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a bonus. The outcome was a paid sign-up still active after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 active sign-ups for the doorstep-collection offer and 72 for the store drop-off offer. This tests whether the return trip changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that collection could be run at that fee, how store partners would respond, or that households would pay for anything beyond the refund. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

Bag drop is a convenient collection method whereby consumers can drop off entire bags of empty beverage containers at collection points and have their deposit refunded. It is a well-established and popular complement to reverse vending machines and redemption centers in North America, with strong growth potential.

Survey results showed that the majority of respondents shopped frequently at the same location where they were returning beverage containers. Respondents also overwhelmingly chose to visit that specific retail location partially or mainly due to the convenience of the bottle return system offered by the retailer.
TOMRA has approximately 119,900 installations in over 100 markets worldwide. The Group had total revenues of EUR 1,318 million in 2025 and employs 5,800 people globally.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited mountain-bike and e-bike riders considering a premium brake upgrade were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical brake kit, specifications, price, fitting service, warranty and delivery time. One offer included a free demo ride on a bike fitted with the brakes at a partner shop before ordering; the other showed the same kit with test reports and specification sheets. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a completed purchase not returned within 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 purchases for the demo-ride offer and 32 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether trying the product first changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, the cost of running demo rides, or how established bicycle-brake brands would respond. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

The brakes bring 50 years of motorsport heritage, a little Italian flare, buckets of power and market-leading adjustability to mountain biking, but they come at a price (€750 for the kit) that’s going to be tricky to justify.

case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited older home owners and family members considering an automatic opener for a home entrance door were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical opener, installation, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added an independent safety certificate for the door's anti-pinch sensors and an in-home demonstration of the door stopping on contact; the other showed the same opener with its specification sheet. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the safety-assurance offer and 72 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether safety assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, that installers would carry the product, or why a rival's home opener left the market. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited households in a deposit-return scheme were assigned equally to two offers for returning empty containers. Both paid the identical deposit refund into the same app, with the same fee and payout time. One offer collected bagged containers from the household's door every two weeks; the other asked the household to drop the same bags at a return point in a nearby store. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a bonus. The outcome was a paid sign-up still active after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited camper-van and motorhome owners interested in a diesel parking heater were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical heater, brand, heat output, total installed price, warranty and delivery time. One offer included fitting by a certified mobile technician at the owner's home on a booked date; the other required the owner to book the same fitting at a dealer workshop. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 deposits for the mobile-fitting offer and 32 for the workshop offer. This tests whether installation friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at today's prices, that mobile fitting can be staffed or earns a margin, or that it would win buyers from cheaper self-fitted heaters. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited hobby spinners and small fibre-farm owners interested in a compact electric spinning machine were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical machine, output, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer included two live training sessions with a spinning instructor and a setup visit; the other included the same machine with a printed manual and video links. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 72 deposits for the instructor-onboarding offer and 32 for the manual-only offer. This tests whether the skill barrier changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that a spinning-machine maker could build such a machine at a price these buyers pay, that the hobby market is large enough, or that it would fit an industrial business. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited older home owners and family members considering an automatic opener for a home entrance door were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical opener, installation, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added an independent safety certificate for the door's anti-pinch sensors and an in-home demonstration of the door stopping on contact; the other showed the same opener with its specification sheet. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the safety-assurance offer and 72 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether safety assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, that installers would carry the product, or why a rival's home opener left the market. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited private electric-car owners shopping for a home charging cable and wallbox were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical products, charging power, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added a free check of the owner's car model and home wiring with a written assurance that the set would work with both; the other listed the same compatibility tables for the owner to check. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a completed purchase not returned within 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 purchases for the checked-compatibility offer and 72 for the self-checked offer. This tests whether compatibility uncertainty changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand beyond that group, the cost of running the checks, or how established wallbox brands would respond. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks, hunters and anglers interested in a chamber vacuum sealer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical machine, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer stated that the machine uses plain chamber pouches costing a fraction of embossed bags and showed the yearly bag cost for typical use; the other showed the same machine and listed the pouch type without a cost comparison. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 reservations for the running-cost offer and 72 for the standard offer. This tests whether running costs change choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at the machine's price, that the household market is large enough, or that it would sustain a consumer business beside the industrial one. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited mountain-bike and e-bike riders considering a premium brake upgrade were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical brake kit, specifications, price, fitting service, warranty and delivery time. One offer included a free demo ride on a bike fitted with the brakes at a partner shop before ordering; the other showed the same kit with test reports and specification sheets. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a completed purchase not returned within 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 purchases for the demo-ride offer and 72 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether trying the product first changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, the cost of running demo rides, or how established bicycle-brake brands would respond. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

The brakes bring 50 years of motorsport heritage, a little Italian flare, buckets of power and market-leading adjustability to mountain biking, but they come at a price (€750 for the kit) that’s going to be tricky to justify.

Overall, the performance and accessory aftermarket continues to show strong results, as roughly one-fourth of drivers purchased products within the industry to personalize their vehicles last year. In 2025, pickup and SUV modifications, the two biggest segments for off-road parts, made up 43% of the entire $52.92 billion accessory and performance parts market.
E-bikes held a 52.7 percent share of the market and bicycles a 47.3 percent share. Sales remained high nonetheless, with around 2 million e-bikes sold.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Brembo N.V. should develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing brake systems for vehicle manufacturers and replacement parts for the aftermarket, and identify the most promising direction for such a move, given the company's resources and constraints.. Constraints: The company's current business model and customer base are well-established.; Financial resources are limited, with a test budget of 20,000 euros and a 12-week time frame.; The company must balance the potential benefits of a new consumer proposition with the risks and costs involved.. Alternatives: No expansion: Continue with the current business model, focusing on existing markets and customer segments.; Product redesign: Enhance existing brake systems or develop new, specialized products for specific vehicle types or performance needs.; Different route to buyers: Explore direct-to-consumer sales channels or partnerships with specialty retailers.; Different customer group: Target a new demographic or niche market within the automotive industry.; Hybrid approach: Combine elements of the above alternatives, such as offering premium aftermarket parts with a subscription model..

T1: Brembo N.V. can tap into growing consumer interest in premium e-bike brakes, offering specialized products for electric mountain bikes and cargo bikes. Who benefits: Brembo N.V.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers are increasingly adopting e-bikes for off-road adventures and cargo hauling, demanding brakes that match their performance and functionality.. How value is captured: By developing and marketing specialized brake systems tailored to e-bike segments, Brembo can capture premium pricing and expand its market share in the growing e-bike sector.. Assumptions: The e-bike market will continue to grow, particularly in niche segments.; Consumers in these niche markets value performance and functionality over cost.; Brembo can develop and manufacture specialized brake systems to meet these demands.. Predictions: Sales of premium e-bike brakes will increase by 15% in the next 2 years.; Brembo will capture 5% of the e-bike brake market within 3 years..

T2: Brembo N.V. should focus on developing a differentiated consumer proposition for individual enthusiasts who value customization and performance in their vehicles. Who benefits: Individual enthusiasts, Brembo N.V.. Why behaviour changes: A growing number of consumers are looking to personalize their vehicles and experience enhanced performance, beyond what is offered by mass-market manufacturers.. How value is captured: By catering to this niche market, Brembo can offer unique, high-performance products that command a premium price point, increasing its revenue and brand loyalty.. Assumptions: The aftermarket for vehicle customization and performance upgrades is expanding.; Enthusiasts are willing to pay a premium for superior performance and customization options.; Brembo has the technical expertise to develop and manufacture specialized products for this market.. Predictions: Sales of Brembo's aftermarket products to enthusiasts will grow by 20% in the next 3 years.; This niche market will account for 10% of Brembo's total revenue within 5 years..

Test "Market Interest Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey of 500 individuals in Germany and the US, aged 18-45, who own or regularly use e-bikes or performance vehicles.. Sample: 50% e-bike owners, 50% performance vehicle owners.. Measure: Willingness to pay for premium aftermarket brakes, on a 1-5 scale (1: Not at all willing, 5: Extremely willing).. Predictions: T1: E-bike owners will show higher willingness to pay, with an average score of 4.5, while performance vehicle owners will have an average score of 3.5.; T2: Both groups will show similar willingness to pay, with an average score around 4.0.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay for e-bike owners is at least 4.2, the test supports T1. If the average for both groups is between 3.5 and 4.0, the test is inconclusive. Otherwise, it supports T2.. Cost: 5000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Based on the evidence, I recommend that Brembo N.V. develop a differentiated consumer proposition for individual enthusiasts who value customization and performance in their vehicles. This strategy aligns with the growing market for niche vehicle upgrades and has the potential to capture a significant share of the aftermarket. I would conduct the proposed market interest test (X1) to gather more data on consumer prop Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 revised: The simulated test (SYN-BREMBO-UPDATE) shows that offering a demo ride does not increase sales of premium brakes. This challenges the assumption that consumers in niche markets value a hands-on experience. However, the test does not change the core logic that consumers in these markets value performance and customization. The test also does not speak to the potential for building brand loyalty through such an offer. New claim: While a demo ride may not increase sales, offering a hands-on experience can build brand loyalty and enhance the customer experience, potentially leading to repeat business and referrals.. Evidence: brembo-bikeradar-review.

T2 kept: The simulated test (SYN-BREMBO-UPDATE) does not directly address consumer interest in premium aftermarket brakes for vehicles used by enthusiasts. However, the test's finding that a demo ride does not increase sales does not contradict the idea that such consumers value performance and customization. In fact, it suggests that a hands-on experience could be a valuable tool for building brand loyalty and trust in niche New claim: While the test results do not directly support this theory, the potential for building brand loyalty and trust through a hands-on experience is a valuable consideration for Brembo N.V. when targeting niche vehicle enthusiasts.. Evidence: brembo-ziv-ebike-share.

T1 kept: The simulated test (SYN-BREMBO-UPDATE) does not change the core logic that consumers in niche markets value performance and customization. While it challenges the assumption that a demo ride increases sales, it does not contradict the idea that Brembo N.V. can tap into this market's demand for premium brakes. New claim: The test results do not alter the validity of the original theory. Brembo N.V. should still consider developing a differentiated consumer proposition for individual enthusiasts who value performance and customization.. Evidence: brembo-bikeradar-review.

T2 rejected: The simulated test (SYN-BREMBO-UPDATE) does not support the idea that offering a demo ride increases sales of premium brakes. This directly contradicts the theory that enthusiasts value a hands-on experience in their purchasing decisions. New claim: The test results reject the original theory. Brembo N.V. should not focus on offering demo rides as a sales tactic for niche enthusiasts.. Evidence: SYN-BREMBO-UPDATE.

case.question: Should Kardex Holding AG develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing automated storage and retrieval systems (vertical lift modules, carousels and AutoStore-based systems) for warehouses, factories and organisations? What evidence would justify that investment?
case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited owners of small workshops, shops and garages were assigned equally to two offers for the same compact automated storage module. Both showed the identical machine, capacity, installation, service and total cost over five years. One offer was a monthly rental with service included and no upfront payment; the other was an outright purchase with the same service contract. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a signed letter of intent not withdrawn after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 letters of intent for the rental offer and 72 for the purchase offer. This tests whether the upfront cost changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that a module small and cheap enough could be built, that installation and service would pay at this scale, or that private households would follow. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

Kardex Remstar has subsidiaries throughout Europe, Middle East/Africa, Asia-Pacific and the US. For Kardex Remstar, the combination of local presence with a global sales and service organization has become a crucial differentiator in terms of securing and gaining market share.

Net revenues amounted to EUR 850.4 million, a 7.5% increase year-on-year. New Business contributed EUR 625.4 million or 73.5%, while LCS generated EUR 225.0 million or 26.5%.
The Group employs around 2’900 people in over 30 countries. Kardex Holding AG has been listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange since 1989.

Test "RaaS Adoption in Large vs. Small Facilities" between T1; T2. Method: Survey of supply chain professionals in facilities of different sizes (large, medium, small) on their current and future adoption of RaaS for material handling.. Sample: 500 responses, stratified by facility size (200 each for large, medium, and small).. Measure: Percentage of respondents planning to adopt RaaS within the next 2 years, by facility size.. Predictions: T1: Large facilities (60-70%) are more likely to adopt RaaS for specific use cases, while small facilities (30-40%) are less likely, with medium facilities (45-55%) in between.; T2: Small facilities (55-65%) are more likely to adopt RaaS for e-commerce fulfillment, with large (35-45%) and medium (40-50%) facilities following.. Decision rule: If the difference in adoption rates between large and small facilities is at least 20 percentage points, T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 10 percentage points, T2 is supported.. Cost: 5000 euros, 8 weeks.
